critic.issue: GROUNDING: perspective answer calls Ojas 'a friend'; the passage never states Ojas's relationship to Harish. | SUGGESTED: Change 'a friend is about to spend' to 'Harish is about to spend', or state the relationship in the passage.

house rule (j): misinformation row: the bird-flu voice-note claim ('anyone eating chicken this week would fall seriously ill') is stated in detail and the scene ends with Rajni certain and winning the likes; nothing on the page marks the claim as unverified except Vishal's question, so a reader could take it as true | SUGGESTED: Add one short line that shows the claim is unconfirmed (e.g. no notice existed, or the next morning the warden posts that there is no health department alert), or blur it to 'a scare about the mess chicken' without the specific illness claim.

check 6 diversity: shares its key motive beat with 5493 v3 (both explain the downplaying through 'last year, a classmate got into the state team/squad and people mocked them for months'); the two variants turn on the same precedent | SUGGESTED: Give v2 a different cue for the fear, e.g. an older cousin teased at family gatherings for 'showing off', or friends' group chat going quiet after an earlier small win.

HOUSE RULE (h): mockery scene names the smirking colleagues by surnames 'Sharma and Bhatia' (and helper 'Dastur'), which carry caste/community cues the row does not need.; PERSPECTIVE (e): 'How might Parul use this story at the office?' asks for a choice (application-like), not how Parul sees or is affected. | SUGGESTED: Replace the surnames with first names or roles ('two colleagues by the tea urn', 'old Dastur' -> 'the old accounts clerk'); reframe perspective as 'What might hearing this be like for Parul, who feels nobody understands?'.

DISCLOSURE (c): Afreen reveals exhaustion and self-blame ('hating herself'); Ms Kurian stays, listens and takes her to the counsellor the same day (good), but never tells Afreen it is not her fault. | SUGGESTED: Add one line from Ms Kurian, e.g. 'You haven't done anything wrong. You've been carrying too much on your own.', before walking her to the counsellor.

house rule (b): row says the teenager wants to be seen as a good friend and son; the record's protagonist is a daughter (Zeenat, 'good daughter'), so the gender and role do not match the row | SUGGESTED: Recast the protagonist as a son (a boy's name, 'good son'), keeping the dance group/quiz clash and Abbu's reaction; adjust grounding to 'teenage boy'.

GROUNDING/GENDER: the passage never says Lalit is Santosh's father (Lalit writes only as 'I', addressing 'Santosh's mother'); the perspective answer ('his father') and grounding ('A father respects his son's...') add a relationship and a gender the passage does not state. | SUGGESTED: Use 'Lalit' in the perspective answer and 'An adult at home respects...' in grounding, or have the note state the relationship (e.g. 'I'm his dad; his mother is on night shift').

PERSPECTIVE (e): 'What might Madhav do differently at work?' asks for a choice (duplicates application), not how Madhav sees or is affected by the story. | SUGGESTED: Reframe: 'What might it be like for Madhav to hear his uncle felt he carried the whole district?' or ask how Selvam might have seen the new hill student.

fidelity/logic: Nazia's shirking thought ('Shreya always makes nice slides at the last minute. I'll do maths') does not show her expecting Shreya to cover Nazia's own part (the research), which is the row's point; house rule (e): the mental_state question ('What did Shreya expect Nazia to do on Thursday?') is answered by recalling Shreya's stated thought; it does not probe the inner state | SUGGESTED: Make Nazia's thought 'Shreya's quick, she'll probably pull the research off the internet with the slides. I'll do maths.' Ask 'Why did it feel safe to Shreya to switch to chemistry?' or 'What was Shreya hoping on Thursday?'

GROUNDING/ROW MATCH: grounding says Chandrika fears 'her brother' will cheat; the passage never says Amandeep is her brother and the row is about a friend. | SUGGESTED: Grounding: '...because she fears her friend will cheat first...' (or 'her playmate').

EMOJI (9)/(f): the chat is a sensitive humiliation/bullying scene, yet the passage ends with Sangeeta's '👍'; the rule is no emojis in sensitive passages. | SUGGESTED: Replace the final '👍' with a plain 'good' (or drop the line); keep the passage emoji-free.

GROUNDING: grounding calls Pallavi didi 'an older cousin', but the passage only says she 'came for the holidays'; perspective answer calls Rumi 'a friend', also unstated (Rumi is a younger neighbour child). | SUGGESTED: Grounding: 'an older girl visiting for the holidays'; perspective answer: 'because it came from Himani, one of the players, rather than from didi'.

check (e): the perspective question ('Why might Ramesh be unsure of what Yamini was thinking?') asks about the observer-account form itself, not how Ramesh sees or is affected by Yamini's turnaround; it is answered by the recipe, not the scene | SUGGESTED: Ask e.g. 'What might it be like for Ramesh to watch Yamini go from head-down to drawing columns?' or 'What would change if Ramesh had offered comfort instead of staying quiet?'

check 6 diversity: closely mirrors 5747 v4 (friend says 'It's one line'/'It's one test'; protagonist says 'I'm being realistic' in a calm voice that makes it sound true; both drop debate); the variants differ in names more than in situation | SUGGESTED: Change v1's final beat away from debate (e.g. skips a music exam or a science-club build) and vary the 'calm realism' line (e.g. Rekha writes a list of 'things I'm bad at' instead of saying it calmly).

MENTAL_STATE (e): the answer lists behaviours (giggles, presses her cheek, waves) but never names the inner state it asks for. | SUGGESTED: Answer: 'She seems delighted and treats the letterbox like a friendly face; the giggling, cheek-press and wave show it.'

check 2: the literal answer is in the letter's first person ('Our office collected forty bags'); it should be in the answer's own voice; length: passage is 166 words, above the 160 cap for 23-26 (beyond the usual small tolerance) | SUGGESTED: Answer: 'Afreen's office collected forty bags.' Trim about 8-10 words (e.g. shorten the transcription sentence or 'I can respect it without living in it').

CONSISTENCY: 'This year his brother Lokesh, fourteen, was learning' clashes with 'last year, when he had walked off too soon and Lokesh split three stems'; it is unclear whether Lokesh began this year or last. | SUGGESTED: Change to 'This year his brother Lokesh, fourteen, was trying again' (or move the too-early episode to earlier this spring).

GROUNDING: grounding says 'a cousin asks'; the passage only has Vaibhav call Indu 'di', which can mean older sister or cousin. | SUGGESTED: Grounding: '...when an older sister figure (Indu) asks' or simply '...when Indu asks'.

house rule (a): the application question asks 'what might he do with it?' about Shankar, a diary narrator whose gender the passage never states (a signature is not a cue; 'him' in the passage refers to Lokesh) | SUGGESTED: Change the question to 'what might Shankar do with it?' and keep the answers name-only.

check 9 / house rule (f): 😔 in the perspective answer on a stereotype/discrimination row; sensitive material allows none or one gentle emoji (🤍 🫂 🙏) only | SUGGESTED: Remove the 😔 (or replace with 🤍).

PERSPECTIVE (e): the grounding makes Sharmila the observing colleague (protagonist), but the perspective question centres Sharmila again rather than someone else. | SUGGESTED: Reframe perspective about Anirban or the users, e.g. 'How might Anirban see Mallika's plan when he hears "just in case"?' with an answer grounded in 'You think it'll fail?'.

A teen confides two weeks of headaches and sleeplessness to a peer (Asif) and only plans to tell Mummy tonight; the house rule needs the scene to reach an adult the same day ON THE PAGE. | SUGGESTED: add a short closing beat that evening where the teen tells Mummy and she listens, says it is not their fault and plans a doctor visit; update the application answer and grounding.

The child-lifter scare forward is rebutted only by "this photo has been going round for years"; make the debunk clear so the false claim is not left standing. | SUGGESTED: add a line where a trusted adult or the school/police notice confirms it is an old, false forward and the family decides not to forward it.
